summary: Enumerated every declared object-store consumer across docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.control.yml/docker-compose.exec.yml and services/**/*.py plus deploy/evidence tooling under scripts/, found zero real S3/MinIO source-code consumers and three real GCS consumers (one in-request-path, two out-of-band), compared local-S3-replacement vs managed-store vs conditional retirement, produced two reproducible isolated proofs (a mocked-bucket round trip and a same-process two-instance local-disk durable read/write verification) against the real adapter, recorded the accepted choice with hosted-content and identity-preservation caveats made explicit, and corrected the core/workers/research/management-ai/execution source-profile contract to match actual docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.control.yml/docker-compose.exec.yml per-environment Compose-topology, dependency-closure, and volume evidence (second reviewer-reject correction pass: see profile_contract_design.corrections_from_second_reviewer_reject below).

required_corrections_and_disposition.finding: storage-consumer-matrix.json:85,101 and storage-topology-decision.md contradicted each other on hosted content: absence of source-code I/O was wrongly presented as proof of an empty/unpopulated hosted MinIO volume or GCS bucket.
required_corrections_and_disposition.fix: Reworded the matrix conclusion, existing_data_volumes block, and every corresponding topology-decision passage to say hosted content is unknown (this task did not inspect it), and made MinIO retirement explicitly conditional on a later hosted inventory/readback check by OSS-OBJECT-STORE-CUTOVER-001, not on this source-only finding.

required_corrections_and_disposition.finding: Incomplete consumer/preserved-contract inventory: scripts/capture_canonical_telemetry_baseline.py:159-183 requires GCS generation/metageneration/pantheon_sha256 metadata; scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh:2038-2051 performs a real GCS PUT/GET/DELETE probe; matrix:98 wrongly dismissed tenant isolation despite services/control-plane/bff/main.py:17354-17383 enforcing session/tenant-scoped attachment-read authorization.
required_corrections_and_disposition.fix: Added both scripts as real_object_store_consumers entries (with exact behavior, identity semantics required, and line refs) in storage-consumer-matrix.json and storage-topology-decision.md §1 finding 3; corrected the retention/tenant block to document the BFF-layer tenant/session authorization contract and require its preservation; corrected the decision's §5 cutover scope to require preserving both the authorization check and the generation/metageneration/pantheon_sha256 identity contract.

required_corrections_and_disposition.finding: The only proof (FakeBucket, in-memory dict) did not establish durable/restore feasibility and conflated it with unknown hosted state.
required_corrections_and_disposition.fix: Added a second, independent isolated proof that exercises the adapter's real local-filesystem fallback path (genuine disk write via os.replace, then read back through a brand-new store instance to rule out an in-process cache hit), seeded with a known SHA-256 and verified byte-for-byte. Documented explicitly that the GCS generation/metageneration/pantheon_sha256 identity contract is NOT proven in isolation (no hosted gcloud credentials available) and left that as an open item for the cutover task rather than fabricating it as proven.

required_corrections_and_disposition.finding: profile-contract.json defects: :25 promoted the explicitly opt-in lifecycle-projector-capacity-benchmark (docker-compose.yml:1519-1528, `profiles: ["lifecycle-capacity-benchmark"]`) into core; :91 defaulted opt-in smoke/e2e harness containers to core; workers (:35-47) activated three research-owned workers (alpha-replication-worker, training-session-preview-worker, policy-learning-shadow-eval-scheduler) as Prod Control singletons even though their hard depends_on targets (research-orchestrator-svc, training-session-svc, policy-learning-svc; docker-compose.yml:381-385,561-563,666-670) are disabled in Prod Control; execution (:80-86) plus the core fallback (:91) omitted broker-adapter/exchange-adapter/pantheon-lean-live and placed signal-store under core even though docker-compose.exec.yml:173-181 requires signal-store+runtime-manager+broker-adapter+exchange-adapter for Prod Execution while Prod Execution disables core.
required_corrections_and_disposition.fix: Moved lifecycle-projector-capacity-benchmark out of core.services into an opt_in_never_default note citing its Compose profile; added an explicit compose-profile carve-out to unclassified_services_default_rule so opt-in harness containers are never implicitly defaulted to core; split workers into core-owned (Prod Control singleton, unchanged) vs a new research_owned_workers_conditional_on_research_profile block for the three affected services, with their own dev/ephemeral_staging/prod_control/prod_execution row matching the research profile; rewrote execution.services as two explicit per-Compose-file lists (dev/ephemeral-staging docker-compose.yml topology vs the isolated Prod Execution docker-compose.exec.yml stack), moved signal-store into execution (it has zero core consumers in docker-compose.yml), added broker-adapter/exchange-adapter to the Prod Execution list and pantheon-lean-live as an explicit opt-in service, corrected dependency_requirements to state docker-compose.exec.yml declares no postgres/nats at all (its own header: excludes control-plane services), and split volume_requirements per compose file (runtime-data only on docker-compose.exec.yml; runtime-data/broker-data/capital-data on the dev/staging docker-compose.yml topology).

artifacts_produced.purpose: Full read-only enumeration of every docker-compose service declaring PANTHEON_S3_* env vars or depends_on minio, the repo-wide non-test search for boto3/botocore/S3-client usage (zero hits), all three real object-store consumers (attachment store, telemetry-baseline recovery-source identity, deploy-time bucket probe), and the corrected hosted-content-unknown / tenant-authorization findings.

Compares the 3 acceptance-bounded options, records the accepted decision (GCS as sole backend; conditionally retire the unused-in-source-code MinIO layer pending hosted inventory), and carries both reproducible isolated proofs (mocked-bucket round trip and real local-disk durable restore/readback).

Design-only core/workers/research/management-ai/execution profile contract with health/dependency/volume/isolation requirements, corrected against actual docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.exec.yml Compose-profile-opt-in and depends_on evidence, aligned to SA.md's accepted environment-identity plan and to the corrected storage decision.

consumer_enumeration.method: grep across docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.control.yml, docker-compose.remote-dev.yml, docker-compose.exec.yml for PANTHEON_S3_ENDPOINT/PANTHEON_ARTIFACT_BUCKET/minio; a repo-wide non-test grep for boto3/botocore/S3 client construction under services/ and scripts/; and a direct read of the three files a prior reviewer identified as additional real GCS consumers.
consumer_enumeration.result: 18 services (main stack) / 12 services (control stack) declare the four PANTHEON_S3_* env vars; only 8/9 of those add a depends_on: minio: condition: service_healthy edge. Zero non-test source files construct an S3 client. The two files that read the env vars (services/foundation/persistence_posture.py, services/source_search_posture.py) only check presence for a staging/prod posture gate and explicitly document that they never open a connection.

options_compared.option: A: replace MinIO with another maintained local S3-compatible server
options_compared.disposition: rejected — no S3-API consumer exists in application source to justify standing up a replacement server; would not help any of the three real GCS consumers

options_compared.option: B: standardize on the existing supported managed object store (Google Cloud Storage)
options_compared.disposition: accepted — already integrated for all three real consumers, already budgeted in RESOURCE_AND_COST_MODEL.md (~$6/month), already proven in isolation (two independent proofs), matches the all-GCP environment-identity plan

options_compared.option: C: documented retirement (no real consumer/data remains)
options_compared.disposition: folded into the accepted decision, scoped to the MinIO/S3 source-code layer only, and made conditional on a later hosted-content inventory confirming nothing populated needs migration/restore before deletion — object storage itself is not retired

profile_contract_design.cross_cutting_rule: no profile's startup health may depend on minio; the accepted GCS path stays env-gated/optional for every profile; deploy-time/release-evidence GCS tooling (scripts/deploy_nonprod_vm.sh, scripts/capture_canonical_telemetry_baseline.py) is out-of-band and does not become a new profile startup dependency
profile_contract_design.corrections_from_reviewer_reject: opt-in lifecycle-capacity-benchmark and smoke/e2e harness containers no longer default to core; signal-store moved from core to execution (its only real docker-compose.yml consumers); three research-owned workers split out of the blanket Prod Control singleton row; execution profile now lists dev/ephemeral-staging (docker-compose.yml) and Prod Execution (docker-compose.exec.yml) services separately, including broker-adapter/exchange-adapter/pantheon-lean-live and a corrected dependency/volume closure with no fabricated postgres/nats dependency on the isolated Prod Execution stack
profile_contract_design.corrections_from_second_reviewer_reject: Added compose_topology_by_environment mapping each SA.md environment to the actual Compose file it runs (docker-compose.yml for dev/ephemeral_staging vs the separate, external-runtime-wired docker-compose.control.yml for prod_control vs docker-compose.exec.yml for prod_execution). Corrected core/workers dependency_requirements to name the real cross-profile hard depends_on edges that exist on docker-compose.yml (telemetry/incidents/evolution/deployment-outbox-consumer -> runtime-manager; operator-bff -> four research services + openclaw-gateway-adapter + paper-fleet-reconciler + runtime-manager) and to state these do not exist on docker-compose.control.yml, which reaches runtime-manager and the OpenClaw adapter only via external URLs -- documenting the gap rather than fabricating an already-clean dependency closure for the dev/ephemeral_staging mono-stack. Removed the circular management-ai/core startup claim: corrected dependency_requirements to state openclaw-gateway-adapter itself has no depends_on edge on any core service, while operator-bff/consultation-svc instead depend on it, so management-ai gates part of core startup rather than the reverse; also documented that this edge does not exist on docker-compose.control.yml. Added bff-data to core.volume_requirements (operator-bff's own volume, previously omitted) and documented its pre-existing cross-profile read-only mount by two workers-profile services. Added activation_clarification_dev_paper to the execution profile explaining that 'dev: NO (Paper)' means Live-broker capability is disabled, not that the Paper-topology runtime-manager/broker/signal-store services are absent from the running dev stack.
